A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LOGGIA routing algorithm and simulation framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison despite reflow and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original packet-level simulations, routing comparisons, generalization experiments, and architectural and training ablations in Sections 5-6 and Appendices C-D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulation results and additionally reports a packet-loss breakdown in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The log-space MPN/Dijkstra policy, imitation pretraining, PPO/MAPPO, adaptive entropy regularization, and early stopping remain. The completed message-passing specification and renaming BC/IL to ILInitial/ILDAgger do not establish a changed implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use mini5, B4, GEANT, and the nx topology family, including generalization to 100 nodes and synthetic mixed TCP/UDP traffic. The new loss analysis uses existing benchmark scenarios.

E2.justification: MAGNNETO, FieldLines, M-Slim, and the shortest-path baselines remain the comparison methods. Figure 6 reports additional outcomes for existing comparators; the renamed imitation-learning variants retain their previous procedures and comparisons.

E3.justification: Figure 6 extends the reported evaluation metrics to total dropped data decomposed into TTL expiration, TCP discards, and buffer overflow. The existing topology, traffic, training-budget, episode, deployment, and delay-scaling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 6 adds a cause-specific packet-loss analysis across four topology presets, examining losses associated with congestion, TCP behavior, and routing loops. The existing architectural, training, buffer-size, control-frequency, and hardware analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 adds 95% bootstrap confidence intervals to Figure 5 and appendix Figures 12-17, supplementing existing boxplots. Both versions already report eight training seeds and 30 evaluation episodes; no increase in repeated runs is stated.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds mean packet-loss results and findings, including TTL-expiration losses only for FieldLines. Existing benchmark boxplots and Tables 3-5 retain their results, including LOGGIA's reported 333.370 MB on B4 and 460.714 MB on GEANT.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects/completes the mathematical MPN specification: v3 Equation (1) explicitly includes both edge endpoints and global features in edge updates, and pooling over nodes and edges in global updates. The MDP formulation, losses, and complexity arguments remain; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: Novelty framing is refined: introduction contribution (ii) emphasizes log-space link prediction instead of a 'new training protocol,' while Section 4 explicitly claims the first combined application of established stabilization techniques to routing. The principal performance, generalization, and deployment claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds concrete qualifications about omitted delays and feasible state-update frequency. v3 also explains FieldLines' TTL losses through routing loops and qualifies buffer-size and control-frequency benefits. However, its new blanket claim that LOGGIA has the lowest neural-method packet losses is contradicted by Figure 6's GEANT bars.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page pointer and Reproducibility Statement covering LOGGIA, the framework, and reproduction/visualization scripts. It also discloses the 64-hop TTL limit and clarifies parallel MPN updates. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time information remain.

R1.justification: Related work gains connections to network-flow and combinatorial optimization, including Khalil, Nazari, Kool, and Dudzik. Additional citations contextualize GNN expressiveness, PPO early stopping, and imitation pretraining, clarifying the contribution as a combination of established techniques.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites expand related work, assumptions, and the algorithm explanation; terminology changes include maximum-entropy to entropy-regularized exploration and BC/IL to ILInitial/ILDAgger. A Reproducibility Statement is added, while the overall section and appendix organization remains.

P2.justification: v3 adds the stacked packet-loss chart, overlays confidence intervals on retained boxplots, and updates legends and captions. Existing figures and tables are renumbered or repositioned under the publication layout; the original schematics and principal plot structures remain.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the confidence intervals and packet-loss diagnosis make uncertainty and failure modes easier to assess. Clearer deployment caveats and code-access information also improve transparency. These are limited gains to an otherwise stable study, partly offset by the new loss-ranking overstatement: Figure 6 shows lower GEANT losses for MAGNNETO than LOGGIA.
